title: No signs of star formation being regulated in the most luminous quasars at z ∼ 2 with ALMA
question: Is star formation in hosts of the most luminous z~2 quasars enhanced or suppressed (regulated), as judged from the intrinsic SFR distribution from ALMA 850um continuum?

data.angular_resolution: ~0.9 arcsec average major beam (7.5 kpc at z=2)
data.sensitivity: requested 0.12 mJy/beam (3 sigma); achieved mean ~0.09 mJy/beam; flux error ~0.1 mJy

what.value: Quasar sample and bolometric luminosities from SDSS DR7 quasar catalog

evidence.quote: We draw our sample from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) DR7 quasar catalog (cite: Schneider:2010; Shen:2011), with $\delta<+15$ deg.

what.value: Median host stellar mass log M*=11.1 (range 10.5-11.5) adopted for the sample

evidence.loc: 4.1 The intrinsic SFR distribution of luminous quasars
evidence.quote: reporting a median stellar mass of $\log \ensuremath{M_\ast}\,/ M_\odot=11.1$, which we here adopt as the average $M_\ast$ of our sample.
we use a simple approach by fitting with a library of SEDs consisting of the three AGN SED temples provided in (cite: Lyu:2017)

evidence.loc: 3.2 FIR luminosities and Star formation rates
evidence.quote: We fix the emissivity index to $\beta=1.6$ and the dust temperature to $T_{\rm d}=47$ K (cite: Beelen:2006)

what.value: MS galaxy IR SED template at z~2

evidence.loc: 3.2 FIR luminosities and Star formation rates
evidence.quote: The second approach uses a characteristic IR SED template of MS galaxies at $z\sim 2$ as provided in (cite: Bethermin:2015).

what.value: Hickox et al. model SFR distribution (mean 2.58, dispersion 0.31) and Magneticum simulation SFRs at z=2

evidence.quote: Their SFR distribution has a mean of 2.58 and a dispersion of 0.31.

recipe.method: Fit point-source or Gaussian (if resolved >3 sigma) models directly to visibilities

recipe.goal: Black hole mass and bolometric luminosity from SDSS spectra
recipe.method: Multi-Gaussian + power-law + Fe template fits to Mg II and C IV; virial MBH from Mg II; Lbol = 3.2 L3000
Chi2 fit of three AGN templates (standard, WDD, HDD; only normalisation free) to UV-mid-IR photometry; best template subtracted from ALMA luminosity
assumptions: Host galaxy negligible in UV-mid-IR; ALMA and Herschel excluded from fit

recipe.method: Modified blackbody normalised to AGN-subtracted 850um flux; alternative MS-galaxy SED template; Kennicutt conversion
key_parameters: beta=1.6, Td=47 K (30-50 K range for uncertainty)
assumptions: Chabrier IMF; 8-1000um LIR; SFR = LIR/1e10 Lsun

recipe.goal: Fit log-normal SFR distribution and compare with MS and models
recipe.method: Bayesian log-normal fit; Monte Carlo with Td~N(47,6 K), 1000 realisations; Shapiro-Wilk test; KS test vs Magneticum; MS from Speagle 2014 at assumed M*

evidence.quote: In total 19 of the 20 targets are detected at $850\mu$m at more than $3\sigma$ at the optical QSO position, 16 of them at more than $5\sigma$.

evidence.loc: 4.1 The intrinsic SFR distribution of luminous quasars
evidence.quote: The SFRs span a range of $35-1513\, M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, with a median value of $180\, M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.

evidence.loc: 3.2 FIR luminosities and Star formation rates
evidence.quote: we find an AGN contribution to $L_{850\mu\mathrm{m}}$ in the range of $3-59\%$, with a median value of 14%.
a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test gives p-values of $p_{\rm KS}=0.14$ and $p_{\rm KS}=0.46$

answer_key.quantity: Spearman r, SFR vs log Lbol
